newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, October 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, October 8.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

*PM Romano Prodi says magistrates can count on full support from the government but majority parties are split after Cesare Salvi, leader of the Democratic party of the Left in the Upper House (PDS), said some methods used by the Milan magistrates have proved dangerous (all).

* PDS leader Massimo D'Alema started talks with all parties to find an agreement over constitutional reforms. PM Prodi said he would support D'Alema heading the bi-cameral commission which is expected to carry out such reforms (all).
*The Constitutional court says it is illegal to reiterate decree-laws, which must be converted into law by parliament within 60 days (all).
*Pope Jean Paul II will be operated today to remove his appendix, amid fierce speculation that there might be something more serious (all).
* PM Prodi is said to have asked Treasury officials to start talks for lira return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (La Repubblica).
* European Commission President Jacques Santer said "No doubts that if Italy goes on like this, it will join EMU in the first group" (La Repubblica).

* The European Commission is expected to open an inquiry over state aid to ailing flag carrier Alitalia. In July state-controlled Iri agreed to a 3 trillion lire recapitalisation to save the company from collapse (Sole 24 Ore).
* Italian Treasury offered a total of 700 million ordinary shares, or 8.75 per cent of the share capital, in the second tranche privatisation of energy giant Eni (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
